# BIAN Rule and Guideline Catalogue

Classified rules used by the BIAN Standards Expert skill. **Rule IDs (`BSE-*`) are internal identifiers of this skill. They are not BIAN identifiers** and must never be presented as such.

- **Baseline:** BIAN v14.0 (Feb 2026). Source keys are defined in [bian-source-registry.md](bian-source-registry.md): `GUIDE` (Semantic API Practitioner Guide V8.1, July 2020), `RN14` (v14.0 Release Notes), `OAS14` (official v14.0.0 OpenAPI files), `REPO-ARCH` (`.github/rules/architectural-standards.md`), `REPO-REQ` (`.github/rules/requirement-standards.md`).
- **Evidence Type values:** `Official` (BIAN states it) · `Derived` (reasoned from official relationships) · `Recommended` (implementation practice) · `Org policy` (this repository's own rules; not BIAN).
- **Descriptive vs prescriptive:** BIAN describes the model; it does not publish a list of normative "must" clauses in the sources reviewed. Rules marked `Official` mean *the artefact definition is official*; the **compliance consequence** of a deviation is a judgement and is therefore marked by Severity, which is configurable (see [bian-validation-framework.md](bian-validation-framework.md) §4). Nothing here is a BIAN certification criterion. BIAN's API Align tool "scores alignment and certification" (bian.org BIAN Portal page); its methodology was not accessible and is **not** replicated here.
- **Row fields:** every row carries ID, Name, Description, Rationale, Applicability, Validation Method, Expected Outcome, Severity, Source, BIAN Version, Evidence Type. Category is the section heading.
- **Default severities** are starting points; adjust per assessment context.

---

## A. Structural rules (Category: Structural)

| ID | Name | Description | Rationale | Applicability | Validation Method | Expected Outcome | Severity | Source | BIAN Ver. | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BSE-STR-01 | One pattern, one asset | A Service Domain applies exactly one Functional Pattern to one asset type for the complete lifecycle. | Defines what an SD is and prevents mixed-responsibility components. | Any SD mapping or architecture review. | Ask: what behaviour on what asset? Check the component does not combine two patterns/assets. | Each mapped component has one primary responsibility that fits one SD. | High | GUIDE §2.4, §3.2.1 | V8.1; unchanged in RN14 | Official |
| BSE-STR-02 | Elemental / right-sized | SDs are elemental: a bank adopts one wholly or not at all; a function that can be partly adopted is not an SD-level partition. | Keeps the standard canonical across deployments. | SD identification; decomposition proposals. | Test whether a proposed split/merge produces a utility function or a partial SD. | No proposal invents sub-SDs or "half" SDs. | Medium | GUIDE Att. B, Fig. 19 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-STR-03 | SD is not a process step | An SD is a functional partition (service centre), not a step in an end-to-end process. | Process-oriented decomposition produces overlapping applications. | Architecture validation. | Check that components named after process steps map to BQs or scenario interactions, not SDs. | Process steps are expressed as scenario interactions or BQ work steps. | High | GUIDE Fig. 19, §2.3 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-STR-04 | One Control Record per SD | Each SD has a single Control Record that carries the information it controls over a lifecycle. | Establishes who owns which business information. | Data ownership; API payload review. | Identify the CR (`CR - ...` tag in `OAS14`); check each data item has one governing SD. | Single owner per business information item; no duplicated mastering across SDs without a stated reason. | High | GUIDE §2.4, §3.2.3; OAS14 | V8.1 / 14.0.0 | Official |
| BSE-STR-05 | Name match is not sufficient | Never select an SD only because its name or a keyword matches. Evaluate documented role, pattern, CR and boundaries. | Names are ambiguous (e.g. Position Keeping vs Financial Accounting vs Current Account). | Every SD recommendation. | Compare at least two candidate SDs on role/CR/operations; record why others were rejected. | Mapping record lists candidates, evidence and rejection reasons. | High | Task requirement; REPO-REQ (no conformance from names) | n/a | Recommended |
| BSE-STR-06 | Capability ≠ Service Domain | A Business Capability states what the bank does; an SD is the standard functional partition that supports it. Mapping is many-to-many and must be read from the Portal. | Prevents conflating organisation capability models with BIAN. | Requirement-to-BIAN mapping. | Check the mapping states capability, BIAN hierarchy level and source separately. | Capability and SD columns are distinct; unverified links are flagged. | Medium | RN14 §3; concepts §2 | 14.0 | Derived |
| BSE-STR-07 | Hierarchy terms not interchangeable | Business Area, Business Domain and Service Domain are distinct from business units, teams, DDD bounded contexts, microservices and API resources. | Avoids false conformance claims. | Documentation review. | Search design text for substituted terms. | Terms used precisely. | Low | GUIDE §3.1; REPO-REQ | V8.1 | Org policy |

## B. Semantic rules (Category: Semantic)

| ID | Name | Description | Rationale | Applicability | Validation Method | Expected Outcome | Severity | Source | BIAN Ver. | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BSE-SEM-01 | Pattern ≠ action term ≠ BQ | Functional Patterns (e.g. Fulfill, Assess, Advise) describe SD behaviour; Action Terms (e.g. Initiate, Retrieve, Execute) describe an operation's purpose; BQs partition the CR. | Frequent source of mislabelling. | All outputs. | Check each term is used in its own sense. | Correct vocabulary. | Medium | GUIDE §3.2.1, §3.2.4, §3.2.5 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-SEM-02 | BQ narrows the Control Record | A BQ identifies a sub-partition of the CR so an operation has one unambiguous purpose, and uses the BQ type of the SD's pattern. | Avoids ambiguous operations such as "execute on account". | BQ mapping; operation design. | Confirm BQ exists for the SD in the target release (OAS14 tag `BQ - ...`); check it is a partition, not a new SD. | Operation = action term + CR (+ BQ). | Medium | GUIDE §3.2.4 | V8.1; BQs changed in 14.0 (RN14 §6) | Official |
| BSE-SEM-03 | Only first-level BQs are standard | BIAN defines first-level BQs; sub-qualifiers are implementer-defined and must be MECE and use the same BQ type. | Marks the boundary of the standard. | Designs with nested qualifiers. | Verify nested qualifiers are labelled as organisation extensions. | Sub-qualifiers recorded as extensions. | Low | GUIDE §3.2.4, Fig. 25 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-SEM-04 | Action term meaning is consistent | An action term means the same thing on the CR and on any BQ; observed effect varies with the SD's functional pattern. | Allows consistent interpretation. | Operation mapping. | Compare operation intent with the term definition; e.g. Initiate creates an instance; Execute acts on an active instance. | Operation intent matches term. | Medium | GUIDE §3.2.5, Att. A | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-SEM-05 | Retrieve/Notify are read-only | Retrieve and Notify do not change instance state. | Supports CQRS-style separation. | API method/side-effect review. | Check no state change or hidden side effect behind retrieval operations. | Retrieval is side-effect free. | High | GUIDE §3.2.5 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-SEM-06 | Operations express dependency, not protocol | A service operation defines a service dependency between SDs; it does not prescribe sync/async, choreography or delays. | Prevents over-reading scenarios as protocols. | Interaction design. | Check protocol decisions are marked organisation-specific. | Protocol choices labelled as design decisions. | Low | GUIDE §3.2.5 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-SEM-07 | Default operations are not mandatory | Default operation sets per pattern are a starting point; not all apply and additional ones may exist. | Avoids false "missing operation" findings. | Gap analysis. | Compare against the SD's actual published operations, not the default list. | Gaps measured vs the SD's published operations only. | Low | GUIDE §3.2.5 | V8.1 | Official |

## C. API rules (Category: API)

| ID | Name | Description | Rationale | Applicability | Validation Method | Expected Outcome | Severity | Source | BIAN Ver. | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BSE-API-01 | One API per SD | Each published Semantic API is the logical interface of exactly one SD. | Keeps API boundary equal to SD boundary. | API alignment. | Check that an API does not mix operations of several SDs. | API maps to one SD. | High | RN14 §11; GUIDE §3.5 | 14.0 | Official |
| BSE-API-02 | Endpoint assembly | Endpoint = SD + CR instance id + optional BQ + optional BQ id + action term. | Predictable resource structure. | Path comparison. | Parse the path segments of the organisation API and compare with `OAS14` paths. | Paths follow the structure or deviations are recorded. | Medium | GUIDE Fig. 25; OAS14 (observed) | 14.0.0 | Official |
| BSE-API-03 | Method per action term (observed) | In `OAS14`: Retrieve/Notify → GET; Initiate/Create/Register/Evaluate/Provide/Activate → POST; Update/Control/Exchange/Execute/Request/Grant/Capture → PUT. | Direct method comparison. | Method alignment. | Compare method and action per operation. Count of PATCH/DELETE in OAS14 = 0. | Methods match, or deviation recorded with reason. | Medium | OAS14 (observed over 258 files) | 14.0.0 | Official |
| BSE-API-04 | Naming as published | SD and BQ resource names are as in the spec (PascalCase, concatenated words, e.g. `DebitandCredit`). | Name drift hides semantic drift. | Resource name review. | Exact-match against `OAS14` paths; flag renamed/obsolete BQ names via the change table. | Names match or mapping table exists. | Low | OAS14; RN14 §6 | 14.0.0 | Official |
| BSE-API-05 | Semantic API ≠ implementation spec | Semantic APIs are classification-level; implementers must add finer decomposition, physical data detail, headers, security and error handling. | Prevents treating the spec as complete. | Any API design. | Check the design adds required operational detail without altering semantics. | Extensions present and traceable. | Informational | GUIDE §3.5 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-API-06 | Error structure | `OAS14` declares responses 200/400/401/403/404/429/500 and error body `HTTPError{status_code,status,message}`. Org rules require a richer envelope. | Error contract comparison. | Error review. | Compare codes and body. | Superset of BIAN structure, or deviation recorded. | Low | OAS14; REPO-ARCH | 14.0.0 | Official (BIAN) / Org policy (envelope) |
| BSE-API-07 | Version traceability | Record BIAN release, API spec version and local extensions in the contract and ADRs. | Enables later diff. | Contract review. | Check `info.version`/metadata or ADR cites release (e.g. 14.0.0). | Release + local version both present. | Medium | OAS14 (`info.version: 14.0.0`); REPO-ARCH | 14.0.0 | Org policy |
| BSE-API-08 | REST/JSON is not conformance | Using REST, JSON or BIAN-like URLs does not establish BIAN alignment. | Core anti-hallucination rule. | Any "is it BIAN?" question. | Require SD, CR/BQ, operation and payload evidence before any alignment status. | No `Compliant` without evidence. | Critical | Task requirement; REPO-REQ; REPO-ARCH | n/a | Recommended |
| BSE-API-09 | Action term in path vs repo guidance | `OAS14` ends paths with the action term. `REPO-ARCH` says not to mechanically place action words in REST resource paths. Both can be satisfied by an adapter layer exposing org-style resources while mapping to BIAN operations. | Real conflict between sources. | Where an org API is proposed with BIAN paths. | Surface the conflict; request an architecture decision. | Decision recorded (BIAN-style paths vs adapter). | Medium | OAS14; REPO-ARCH | 14.0.0 | Derived |
| BSE-API-10 | Only SDs with operations have APIs | 16 SDs in v14.0 have no operations and no API. | Avoid fabricating endpoints. | API mapping. | Check the SD against the list in concepts §9. | No API claimed for those SDs. | High | RN14 §11; OAS14 | 14.0 | Official |
| BSE-API-11 | Extensions are additive | Extensions should add attributes/operations without removing or changing the meaning of BIAN ones. | Keeps interoperability. | Customised APIs. | Diff extended vs BIAN spec. | Only additions; removals documented as deviations. | Medium | GUIDE §3.5; REPO-ARCH | V8.1 | Recommended |

## D. Data rules (Category: Data)

| ID | Name | Description | Rationale | Applicability | Validation Method | Expected Outcome | Severity | Source | BIAN Ver. | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BSE-DAT-01 | No invented attributes | BIAN attribute, object and enum names must be read from the SD's spec or Portal, never guessed. | Prevents fabricated standards. | Any data mapping. | Each cited BIAN attribute has a file/schema reference. | All BIAN names are traceable. | Critical | Task requirement; OAS14 | 14.0.0 | Recommended |
| BSE-DAT-02 | CR ≠ whole BOM | The CR is what the SD governs; the BOM is the wider business-object model. Not every BOM field belongs in a given CR or payload. | Avoids over-sized payloads and wrong ownership. | Payload and ownership design. | Check payload attributes against the action-term-filtered attribute list. | Payload fields trace to the SD's operation schema. | Medium | GUIDE §3.2.3, §3.5 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-DAT-03 | Enumeration alignment | Where an org attribute is an enumeration, compare value sets with the BIAN enum (case/format as published). | Value drift breaks interoperability. | Enum mapping. | Diff value sets; classify as equal / subset / superset / different. | Differences recorded. | Medium | OAS14 | 14.0.0 | Official |
| BSE-DAT-04 | ISO 20022 mapping provenance | Only state an ISO 20022 mapping if the BIAN file carries it; otherwise label it a proposed integration mapping. | Avoids false official mappings. | Payments/messaging. | Look for ISO 20022 references in the ISO-extended flavour; otherwise mark `Architecture recommendation`. | Official vs proposed mappings separated. | High | GUIDE §4.2.1; OAS14 ISO flavour | 14.0.0 | Official |
| BSE-DAT-05 | Money and date semantics | In `OAS14` payment `Amount` is `AmountValue` (string, format `Value`) + `AmountCurrency` (`Currencycode`, ISO 4217 per description); payment dates are typed (`PaymentDateType`: e.g. RequestedExecutionDate, ValueDate). | Typed values avoid ambiguity. | Payment payloads. | Compare structure. | Currency explicit; date types explicit. | Medium | OAS14 PaymentOrderInitiation | 14.0.0 | Official |
| BSE-DAT-06 | Identity mapping | Map BIAN identifiers to internal identifiers explicitly (e.g. `paymentorderinitiationid`). | Keeps lifecycle semantics. | Adapter design. | Mapping table exists. | Explicit mapping. | Medium | REPO-ARCH | n/a | Org policy |

## E. Architectural rules (Category: Architectural)

| ID | Name | Description | Rationale | Applicability | Validation Method | Expected Outcome | Severity | Source | BIAN Ver. | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BSE-ARC-01 | Scenarios are illustrative | Business Scenarios are archetypal, non-prescriptive, loosely coupled, non-exhaustive; they are not part of the formal standard. | Prevents reading a scenario as mandatory sequence. | Scenario work. | Check no finding says "must follow scenario X". | Scenario use framed as guidance. | High | GUIDE §3.1, §3.3 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-ARC-02 | Connection = one operation | A first-order connection is one dependency between one calling and one called SD using one operation (action term + optional BQ). | Precise interaction modelling. | Sequence diagrams. | Every arrow names caller, callee and operation. | Arrows are operation-level. | Medium | GUIDE §3.2.6 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-ARC-03 | Overlap and gap detection | Compare component responsibilities pairwise against SD roles/CRs; record overlaps and uncovered responsibilities. | Core of architecture validation. | Architecture review. | Responsibility matrix. | Overlaps/gaps listed with evidence. | High | Derived from BSE-STR-01/04 | 14.0 | Derived |
| BSE-ARC-04 | Do not force-fit | Do not map an existing application to BIAN boundaries without examining its actual responsibilities. | Avoids forced alignment. | Legacy review. | Evidence per mapping. | Unmappable parts flagged `UNMAPPED`/`EXTENDED`. | Medium | Task requirement; REPO-REQ | n/a | Recommended |
| BSE-ARC-05 | Events | V8.1 treats SD event triggering as a proposed extension. v14.0.0 provides AsyncAPI files per SD. Use the SD's AsyncAPI channels as the official event vocabulary; label anything else proposed. | Separates official from invented events. | Event-driven design. | Cross-check channels in the SD's AsyncAPI. | Each event is `Official` (cited) or `Proposed`. | Medium | GUIDE §3.6; OAS/Async 14.0.0 | V8.1 / 14.0.0 | Official |
| BSE-ARC-06 | No deployment implication | An SD is a logical boundary; it does not imply one microservice, database, team or deployment. Boundaries for transactions and orchestration must be designed and documented. | BIAN is implementation-agnostic. | Microservice design. | Deployment mapping table. | SD→bounded context→deployment mapping documented. | Medium | GUIDE §3.5; REPO-ARCH | V8.1 | Official + Org policy |
| BSE-ARC-07 | Anti-corruption boundary | Use an adapter between BIAN contracts and internal models. | Isolates change (e.g. BQ renames). | Integration. | Adapter exists or is planned. | Mapped, versioned adapter. | Medium | REPO-ARCH | n/a | Org policy |
| BSE-ARC-08 | Coupling | Prefer a small number of well-defined operation dependencies; flag SDs that call many others or are called for unrelated purposes. | Detects hidden coupling. | Interaction analysis. | Count distinct callee SDs/operations per component. | Documented, justified dependencies. | Low | Recommended | n/a | Recommended |

## F. Version and lifecycle rules (Category: Lifecycle)

| ID | Name | Description | Rationale | Applicability | Validation Method | Expected Outcome | Severity | Source | BIAN Ver. | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BSE-LIF-01 | Declare the release | State the BIAN release (default v14.0) and the artefact version for every definition. | Content changes between releases. | Always. | Every output cites release. | Release stated. | High | Task requirement; RN14 | 14.0 | Recommended |
| BSE-LIF-02 | No obsolete SDs | Do not recommend an SD that is Obsolete in the target release; mention BIAN's stated replacement. | Lifecycle correctness. | SD selection. | Check [bian-release-14-changes.md](bian-release-14-changes.md) §1.2. | No obsolete SD recommended. | High | RN14 §4.2 | 14.0 | Official |
| BSE-LIF-03 | Use current names | Map old names to the renamed SD/BQ (e.g. Payment Initiation → Payment Order Initiation). | Prevents stale vocabulary. | Legacy docs. | Check change table. | Current names used, old names noted. | Medium | RN14 §4.3, §6.2 | 14.0 | Official |
| BSE-LIF-04 | Replaced/deleted BQs | Do not rely on deleted or replaced BQs. | BQ drift. | BQ mapping. | Check change table §3. | No deleted BQ used. | Medium | RN14 §6.1, §6.3 | 14.0 | Official |
| BSE-LIF-05 | Pattern changes | Re-derive CR/BQs when an SD changed pattern. | Pattern drives CR/BQ type. | Affected SDs. | Check §2 of change table. | Current pattern used. | Medium | RN14 §5 | 14.0 | Official |
| BSE-LIF-06 | Source age | Treat GUIDE V8.1 (2020) as foundational explanation only; newer artefacts override. | Conflicts exist (concepts §12). | All. | Record any conflict. | Conflicts logged. | Medium | Source registry | n/a | Recommended |
| BSE-LIF-07 | Replacement may be absent | A BIAN-named replacement SD may be new and have no API (e.g. Payment Settlement); do not fabricate its operations. | Honesty about availability. | Payment designs. | Check `bian-v14-service-domain-index.md`. | Replacement noted; availability `Unverified`. | Medium | RN14 §4; OAS14 | 14.0 | Official |

## G. Implementation guidelines (Category: Implementation)

| ID | Name | Description | Rationale | Applicability | Validation Method | Expected Outcome | Severity | Source | BIAN Ver. | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BSE-IMP-01 | Map legacy by responsibility | Map legacy modules to SDs by what they do, using scenarios to expose gaps; wrap rather than rewrite where sensible. | GUIDE §4.3.1 describes legacy wrapping. | Legacy programmes. | Responsibility-to-SD table. | Evidence-based mapping. | Informational | GUIDE §4.3.1 | V8.1 | Official |
| BSE-IMP-02 | Avoid fragmentation | Do not create one service per BQ or per operation; group by the SD boundary unless there is a justified reason (scale, ownership). | Prevents chatty designs. | Microservice design. | Count services per SD. | Rationale documented for any split. | Low | Recommended | n/a | Recommended |
| BSE-IMP-03 | Record deviations | Record extensions, exclusions and unmapped capabilities; use status `ALIGNED`, `EXTENDED`, `UNMAPPED`, `NOT_APPLICABLE` (repo vocabulary). | Traceability. | All mappings. | Status per mapping. | Complete mapping log. | Medium | REPO-REQ | n/a | Org policy |
| BSE-IMP-04 | No certification claims | Do not claim BIAN certification or official compliance; any score is an internal metric. | Avoid misleading claims. | Reports. | Wording check. | Disclaimers present. | High | Task requirement; bian.org Portal page | n/a | Recommended |
| BSE-IMP-05 | Org extensions | Organisation-specific attributes/operations must be labelled `Organisation extension`. | Separates official from local. | All outputs. | Label present. | Labelled. | Low | Task requirement | n/a | Recommended |
